title: Networks & Topologies: Addresses & Protocols
welcome_lead: Packets, MAC addresses, IPs and the rules they follow.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on MAC vs IP, packet switching and protocols.
final_note: You can explain how packets find their way across the internet.

concepts.def: Unique hardware ID burned into a device.
Logical address used to route data.
A small chunk of a message sent over a network.
Sending data as packets via varied routes.

walkthroughs.body_html: MAC is like the serial number of a network card — fixed. IP is like a delivery address — changes if you move to a new network. Both work together to deliver data.
A message is split into packets. Each packet may take a different route, then they're reassembled at the destination. If one is lost, only that packet is resent — efficient.

• HTTP/HTTPS: web pages (S = secure)
  • FTP: file transfer
  • SMTP: sending email
  • TCP/IP: underlies almost everything
